findings.title: No test covers the round-robin fixed-host date-override fix
findings.body: The PR description states the primary bug fix is that 'date overrides of fixed hosts are taken into account for round-robin events' (Fixes #8207, #8273). The only test added (lines 786-804) re-runs the existing personal-event 'Check for Date overrides' scenario with a different invitee timezone. There is no test that creates a round-robin event with a fixed host, adds a date override for that fixed host, and asserts that the returned slots are restricted to the fixed host's override. Without such a test the main advertised fix is unverified and could regress silently.

findings.title: checkIfIsAvailable workingHours check has duplicated start/end computation
findings.body: Inside checkIfIsAvailable the new workingHours branch computes `const start = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` and then `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` -- both variables are identical (copy-paste of the same expression). The subsequent guard `if (start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime)` therefore only checks the slot's start time against both bounds and never validates that the slot actually fits inside the working window. A slot starting 30 minutes before the configured end of the working hours (e.g. start 17:30 with workingHour.endTime 18:00 and eventLength 60) would be wrongly accepted. To check whether the slot fits, `end` must be the slot end (slotStartTime + eventLength) or the comparison must be expressed as `slotEnd > workingHour.endTime`.

findings.title: checkIfIsAvailable mixes UTC and local timezones when matching override date to slot date
findings.body: `slotStartTime = time.utc()` (UTC) is compared via `slotStartTime.format('YYYY MM DD')`. The other side, `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').format('YYYY MM DD')`, uses `dayjs(date.start)` (parsed in the server's local timezone) plus an offset, and then formats in the server's local timezone. On any server whose local timezone is not the same as `organizerTimeZone` (or UTC) the two formatted dates can disagree for slots at the boundary of a day, causing date overrides to be ignored or applied to the wrong day. Both sides must be normalized to the same timezone (e.g. `dayjs.utc(date.start).tz(organizerTimeZone).format(...)` on the left, and `slotStartTime.tz(organizerTimeZone).format(...)` on the right).

findings.title: checkIfIsAvailable uses side effects inside Array.find and only honors the first matching date override
findings.body: The new code reuses `Array.prototype.find` to set the outer `dateOverrideExist` flag as a side effect while also using its return value to decide whether the slot is inside the override. As soon as the first matching override returns `true` (slot outside that override), the remaining overrides are skipped. For a user with several date overrides on the same day (e.g. one morning, one afternoon) only the first is consulted, so a slot that lies inside the second override but outside the first is wrongly classified. The mutation of `dateOverrideExist` from inside `find` is also fragile and easy to break in future refactors. The override matching should be written as an explicit loop or `Array#some`/`every` without mutating shared state.

findings.title: checkIfIsAvailable compares day/hour/minute in UTC against organizer's working hours
findings.body: `slotStartTime = time.utc()` puts the slot in UTC, so `slotStartTime.day()`, `slotStartTime.hour()` and `slotStartTime.minute()` return UTC values. The `workingHour` records, however, are expressed in the organizer's timezone (their `days` array and `startTime`/`endTime` in minutes since organizer-local midnight). With any non-zero UTC offset this check is wrong: e.g. an organizer in IST with working hours 09:30-18:00 IST would see a slot at 04:30 UTC (=10:00 IST, inside working hours) produce UTC day/hour = previous-day/04, which does not match `workingHour.days.includes(...)` and `start < workingHour.startTime` is false but the wrong-day branch will be exercised. The slot must be converted to organizerTimeZone (`slotStartTime.tz(organizerTimeZone)`) before reading day/hour/minute.

findings.title: Date override offset uses Date.toString() and reparses in the server's local timezone
findings.body: The new override offset calculation is `const organizerUtcOffset = dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset();`. `override.start` is already a Date; calling `.toString()` produces a locale-dependent representation which dayjs then parses using the server's local timezone. On a server whose local timezone is not UTC this shifts the underlying moment in time, and consequently the `utcOffset()` (which depends on the moment, e.g. across DST boundaries) can be computed at the wrong instant. The same pattern is used for `inviteeUtcOffset`. Use the Date directly: `dayjs(override.start).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()` (or `dayjs.utc(override.start).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()` to be unambiguous).

findings.title: dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, ...) computed four times per entry
findings.body: The new override branch evaluates `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, 'minute')` twice and the equivalent expression for `override.end` twice (lines 219-223). With many overrides per day this multiplies the cost unnecessarily and also makes the four expressions easy to drift out of sync in future edits. Compute each adjusted moment once and reuse it for both `.hour()`/`.minute()` and the equality check.

findings.title: Strict-equality on dayjs objects depends on undocumented valueOf
findings.body: The new date-override zero-length guard uses `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes') === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, 'minutes')`. Two freshly constructed dayjs instances are never `===` unless their `valueOf()` (millisecond timestamp) is equal, which is true here only because dayjs forwards valueOf to the underlying timestamp. This works but is non-obvious and breaks if dayjs is ever replaced or if `add` introduces sub-millisecond precision differences. Use `.isSame(other, ...)` or compare `valueOf()` explicitly.
